Take it when going alone would otherwise be dangerous.|Inventory|BotW}} also known as {{Term/Store|Fighter's Sword|Fighter's Swords|ALttP|plural}},{{Exp Game|ALttP}}{{Cite Book|quote= |book= E |publisher= |page= 140 {{Exp Game|ALttP}}}} and {{Term/Store|Sword of the Hero|Swords of the Hero|TotK|plural}},{{Exp Game|TotK}}{{Cite|{{Big|Sword of the Hero}}
A sword once wielded by a hero in an ancient age. When it's grasped, a strange sense of nostalgia washes over you. Take it when going alone would otherwise be dangerous.|Inventory|TotK}} are recurring [[Item]]s in {{TLoZ Series}}. ==Location and Uses== {{TWW Item Properties/Store |type = Sword }} ==={{TLoZ|-}}=== First appearing in {{TLoZ}}, the Sword can be obtained in a [[Cave]] in the very first area of the game. Inside, [[Link]] finds an [[Old Man]] who tells him to take the Sword because it is dangerous to travel alone.{{Cite|IT'S DANGEROUS TO GO ALONE! TAKE THIS.|Old Man|TLoZ}} The Sword has two additional color variants which appear when Link wears either the [[Blue Ring]] or the [[Red Ring]]. The Sword can damage almost every enemy, but it is one of the weakest items in the game. However, the Sword can be replaced by the [[White Sword]] and then the [[Magical Sword]], which each deals twice the damage of its predecessor. A Sword that is designed like a {{Wp|rapier}} is depicted on the Title Display of the game. It is not confirmed to be any of the Swords that can be obtained in the game. ==={{ALttP|-}}=== {{Stub|ALttP}} {{Descriptions ALttP}} The Fighter's Sword is given to [[Link]] by his Uncle along with the [[Fighter's Shield]] as he enters [[Hyrule Castle (Dungeon)|Hyrule Castle]]. Link uses the Fighter's Sword until he obtains the [[Master Sword]]. During the credits, Link's Uncle is shown using the Fighter's Sword again. ==={{LA|-}}=== {{Descriptions LA}} The Sword in {{LA}} is the first Sword that Link can obtain. It is from Link's [[The Legend of Zelda (Series)|previous adventures]] and has his name engraved on it.{{Cite|You found your {{Color LANS|Pink|sword}}! It must be yours because it has your name engraved on it!|Game Screen|LANS}} Link finds it on [[Toronbo Shores]] shortly after waking up after his crash on [[Koholint Island]]. By bringing 20 [[Secret Seashell]]s to the [[Seashell Mansion]], Link can replace it with the [[Level 2 Sword]].{{Cite|I am the spirit of the mansion. I have been waiting for someone to overcome the darkness. Find all the secret shells and go through the gate to receive the ultimate sword!|Spirit of the Mansion|LADX}}{{Cite Book|quote= |book= E |publisher= |page= 129}} By holding his Sword out, Link can move while he keeps facing the same direction.{{Cite Manual|quote= |game= LA|page= 18}} If Link then releases his Sword, he will perform a [[Whirling Blade]] attack,{{Cite|'The Whirling Blade technique has been handed down from generation to generation by the family of the hero. To use it, hold down the Sword Button and build up your power. When you have enough, you can release the Button! Can you master this?'|Secrets Of The Whirling Blade|LADX}} which deals more damage than a regular Sword blow.{{Cite Manual|quote= |game= LA|page= 19}} Link can also hit walls with his Sword to determine whether or not they can be destroyed using [[Bomb]]s.{{Cite|Well that was a surprise! Hey! I'll tell you a secret! Use your sword to poke at dungeon walls... If you hear a hollow clank, you can break the wall with a Bomb!|Talking Timber|LADX}} ==={{OoS|-}} and {{OoA|-}}=== {{Stub|OoS, OoA}} {{Descriptions OoX}} ==={{TFH|-}}=== The Sword in {{TFH}} is the Sword used by the [[Links]].{{Cite Web|quote= {{Exp|Sword|剣}} |author= Nintendo |published= n.d. |retrieved=August 23, 2017|url= https://www.nintendo.co.jp/3ds/ea3j/world/index.html |title= ゼルダの伝説　トライフォース３銃士 : 冒険ははるか長い道のり {{!}} ニンテンドー3DS {{!}} 任天堂 |site= Official Japanese Site |type= Image }} It changes appearance when certain Outfits are worn, such as the [[Sword Suit]], the [[Sword Master Suit]], the [[Dapper Spinner]], the [[Hero's Tunic]], [[Ninja Gi]], the [[Spin Attack Attire]] and the [[Tri Suit]]. While wearing the [[Fierce Deity Armor]], the Sword becomes the [[Fierce Deity Sword]]. In addition, the Sword becomes a [[Telescope]] while wearing [[Linebeck's Uniform]], and a parasol while wearing the [[Lady's Ensemble]]. ==={{BotW|-}}=== {{BotW Item Properties/Store |type = Weapon |strength = 22 |durability = 27 |flammable = No |magnetic = Yes |buoyant = No |conductive = Yes |guardian = No |throw = Yes |throw_effect = }} The Sword in {{BotW}} can be obtained randomly from a [[Treasure Chest]] dropped by scanning {{TLoZ|-}} [[Link]] [[amiibo]] with the [[Amiibo (Ability)|amiibo]] [[Rune]]. It is described as a Sword that was once wielded by a hero in an ancient age. Its appearance resembles its design throughout the artwork of {{TLoZ|-}}. Being made of metal, the Sword will conduct [[Electricity]] attract [[Lightning]] during [[Thunderstorm]]s. It will sink if it is dropped in [[Water (Terrain)|Water]], but it can be picked up again and manipulated using the [[Magnesis]] Rune. It is also unable to burn when exposed to [[Fire]] or a [[Scorching Climate]]. {{BotW Weapon Parameters |ActorName = "Weapon_Sword_058" |Life = 27 |Power = 22 |SpHitActor = "" |SpHitRatio = 2.0 |IsHammer = false |IsWeakBreaker = false |IsBoomerang = false |IsLuckyWeapon = false |IsPikohan = false |IsThrowingWeapon = true |IsThrowingBreakWeapon = true |ThrowRange = 5.0 |ChemicalEnergyMax = 0 |ChemicalEnergyAmountUsed = 0 |ChemicalEnergyRecoverRate = 0.0 |ChemicalEnergyRecoverInterval = 60 |ShootBeam = "" |SharpWeaponAddAtkMin = 5 |SharpWeaponAddAtkMax = 8 |SharpWeaponAddLifeMin = 3 |SharpWeaponAddLifeMax = 6 |SharpWeaponAddCrit = true |PoweredSharpAddAtkMin = 9 |PoweredSharpAddAtkMax = 14 |PoweredSharpAddLifeMin = 7 |PoweredSharpAddLifeMax = 14 |PoweredSharpAddThrowMin = 1.5 |PoweredSharpAddThrowMax = 2.0 |ThrowSpeed = 1.0 |ThrowRotSpeed = 50.0 |SellingPrice = 5 |BuyingPrice = 20 }} ==={{TotK|-}}=== {{TotK Item Properties/Store |type = One-Handed Weapon |strength = 17 |durability = |flammable = No |magnetic = |buoyant = No |conductive = Yes |guardian = |throw = |throw effect = }} {{Compendium/Extract/TotK|Sword of the Hero}} {{Stub|TotK}} Swords of the Hero can be obtained in {{TotK}} by scanning the [[amiibo#30th Anniversary Link|{{TLoZ|-}} 30th Anniversary Link amiibo]]. The [[Treasure Chest]] that the amiibo provides has a random chance{{Clarify|TotK|reason= What percentage?}} of containing a Sword of the Hero. ==={{EoW|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= EoW |type= Items |category= Items in Echoes of Wisdom |needs= Detailed information on the following: * Who uses Swords * Characteristics of Link's Sword }} {{Stub|EoW}} [[Link]] wields the [[Swordsman's Blade]] while rescuing [[Zelda]] from [[Ganon]]. Later, Zelda obtains the [[Mysterious Sword]] from defeating Link in the [[Suthorn Ruins]], which grants her the [[Swordfighter Form]]. She is also able to use the Swordsman's Blade. [[Sword Moblin]]s also utilize Swords. ==Other Appearances== ==={{TLoZ|-}} (TV Series)=== {{Noncanon|Start}} In the "[[Stinging a Stinger]]" episode of {{TLoZ (TV Series)}}, [[Sleezenose]] offers [[Link]] a Sword as a sign of gratitude for having saved him.{{Cite Episode|quote= Say, you're one hot swordsman. Which reminds me, I have just the gift for you for saving my life.|name= Sleezenose|show= The Legend of Zelda|episode= 9}} Although Link first hesitates to trade it in for his [[Crissword]],{{Cite Episode|quote= Gee, I don't know. It's been a pretty good sword.|name= Link|show= The Legend of Zelda|episode= 9}} Sleezenose explains that anyone who carries the Sword is made irresistible to women, especially princesses.{{Cite Episode|quote= Yes, but this sword is much better. For instance, it makes whoever carries it irresistible to ladies. If you know what I mean. [...] ESPECIALLY princesses.|name= Sleezenose|show= The Legend of Zelda|episode= 9}} This convinces Link and causes him to immediately hand over his old Sword when he hears [[Princess Zelda]] screaming for help.{{Cite Episode|quote= It's a deal! Oh boy!|name= Link|show= The Legend of Zelda|episode= 9}} When Link finds Zelda, she is being attacked by a [[Patra]].{{Cite Episode|quote= Eeh! Get away from me, you stupid Patra! Link! Link! Where are you?|name= Princess Zelda|show= The Legend of Zelda|episode= 9}} The young hero, confident about his new Sword, faces an incoming Patra, but one beam from the foe breaks the Sword in half and causes Link to collapse from the attack. When he looks up and sees the broken Sword, he realizes that he has been tricked by Sleezenose. Link leaves behind the broken Sword when [[Ganon]] appears and captures him. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{TFoE|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Descriptions TFoE}} [[File:TFoE Sword Sprite.png|left]] In {{TFoE}}, the Sword is used as Link's main weapon.{{Cite Manual|quote= The Sword Attack by pressing Button One to strike enemies. It is rumored that hidden in Koridai are ways to make your sword fire deadly Power Blasts.|game= TFoE|page= 3}} As well as being used to fight enemies with, it is also used to pick up dropped items and talk to characters by striking them. In the game's tutorial, the Sword is also referred to as a "'''Smart Sword'''", and it is explained that it will not hurt friendly characters but instead encourage them to talk.{{Cite|Luckily, I brought my Smart Sword. It won't hurt anyone friendly. In fact, it makes them talk!|Link|TFoE}} Link can later receive a stronger Sword called the [[Power Sword]], which replaces his standard Sword. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{TWoG|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Descriptions TWoG}} In {{TWoG}}, the Sword is used as [[Princess Zelda|Zelda]]'s main weapon.{{Cite Manual|quote= The Sword Attack by pressing Button One to strike enemies. It is rumored that hidden in Gamelon are ways to make your sword fire deadly Power Blasts.|game= TWoG|page= 4}} Identically to {{TFoE|-}}, it is also able to pick up items and encourage characters to talk, in addition to fighting enemies with. The Sword is also referred to as a "Smart Sword" in the game's tutorial.{{Cite|Luckily, I brought my Smart Sword. It won't hurt anyone friendly. In fact, it makes them talk!|Zelda|TWoG}} As in {{TFoE|-}}, Zelda can later find the stronger Power Sword. It replaces her standard Sword. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{LA|-}} (Cagiva)=== {{Noncanon|Start}} In the {{LA (Cagiva)}}, [[Link]] finds his lost Sword at [[Toronbo Shores]] after waking up from the shipwreck. During the fight against the [[Angler Fish]], Link breaks the Sword after stabbing the boss on its head. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{BSTLoZ|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|BSTLoZ}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==Nomenclature== {{Nomenclature}} ==Trivia== *In {{TLoZ}}, when the [[Old Man]] gives [[Link]] the Sword, he tells Link the line, "IT'S DANGEROUS TO GO ALONE! TAKE THIS." This line has become a famous line throughout the Zelda fanbase, even being referenced in Zelda media, like {{HW}}, where [[Impa]] references the line when talking to [[Zelda]].{{Cite|Princess Zelda, it's dangerous to go alone. Take me!|Impa|HWDE}} **In {{BotW|-}}, the line is also referenced in the Sword's [[Inventory]] description. ==Gallery== {{All Images}} {{Gallery}} ==See Also== * {{Term|Series|Sword Get Fanfare|link}} * {{Term|Series|Weapon|link}} {{Ref}} {{Categories |Swords, Weapons |items= TLoZ, LA, LADX, LANS, TFH, BotW, TotK, EoW, TLoZ (TV Series), TFoE, TWoG, LA (Cagiva), BSTLoZ }}
